'''Robert E. Ireland''' (1929 – February 4, 2012) was an American chemist and the Thomas Jefferson Chair Professor of chemistry at the [[University of Virginia]]. He is known for his textbook ''Organic Synthesis''<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = White | first = J. D.
 | date = May 1970
 | doi = 10.1021/ed047pa391.1
 | issue = 5
 | journal = Journal of Chemical Education
 | page = A391
 | publisher = American Chemical Society (ACS)
 | title = Organic Synthesis (Ireland, Robert E.)
 | type = Book review
 | volume = 47| bibcode = 1970JChEd..47..391W
 }}</ref> and his contributions to the [[Ireland–Claisen rearrangement]] chemical reaction.<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = McFarland | first1 = Christopher M.
 | last2 = McIntosh | first2 = Matthias C.
 | contribution = The Ireland–Claisen Rearrangement (1972–2004)
 | date = February 2007
 | doi = 10.1002/9783527610549.ch4
 | isbn = 9783527610549
 | pages = 117–210
 | publisher = Wiley
 | title = The Claisen Rearrangement: Methods and Applications}}</ref><ref name="ACS">{{cite news |last1=Ainsworth |first1=Susan |title=Robert E. Ireland |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i16/Robert-E-Ireland.html |access-date=4 May 2022 |magazine =Chemical & Engineering News|volume=90  |issue=16|date=April 16, 2012}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Ireland earned his A.B. in chemistry in 1951 at [[Amherst College]] and earned his Ph.D. in chemistry in 1954 from the [[University of Wisconsin]] with [[William Summer Johnson]], and did his postdoctoral work at [[UCLA]] with [[William Gould Young]]. In 1956, he joined the chemistry department of [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Marshall |first=James A. |date=July 2, 2012 |title=Robert E. Ireland (1929 – 2012) |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201203366 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=51 |issue=27 |pages=6564 |doi=10.1002/anie.201203366 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1965, he became a professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. In 1985 he became the director of the [[Merrell Dow]] Research Institute in [[Strasbourg, France]]. A year later, he became the chair of the chemistry department of [[University of Virginia]].<ref name="ACS"/><ref name="Amherst Obituary">{{cite magazine |title=Robert E. Ireland '51 |magazine= Amherst Magazine |url=https://www.amherst.edu/amherst-story/magazine/in_memory/1951/robertireland |publisher=Amherst College |access-date=4 May 2022|first=Dick|last=Snodgrass}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wipf |first1=Peter |title=Robert E. Ireland |url=http://www.orgsyn.org/content/pdfs/bios/Ireland.pdf |publisher=Organic Syntheses|access-date=4 May 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*[[Ernest Guenther Award]], 1977<ref name="ACS"/><ref name="Amherst Obituary"/>

==Personal life==
Ireland was married to wife Margaret at the time of his passing. He had two sons, Mark and Richard, with his first wife, Suzanne.<ref name="ACS"/><ref name="Amherst Obituary"/>
